topic: What happens if you drink only soda?
title: What drinking only soda does
hook: What happens if you drink only soda?

beats.label: 1 CAN
beats.line: One can of cola packs about ten teaspoons of sugar.

beats.label: 2 CANS
beats.line: Two cans spike your blood sugar, and your body pumps out insulin.

beats.label: 3 CANS
beats.line: Three cans bathe your teeth in sugar and acid, wearing down enamel.

beats.label: 4 CANS
beats.line: Four cans add over five hundred calories, and weight can creep up.

beats.label: 6 CANS
beats.line: Six cans by bedtime, and the caffeine can keep you wide awake.

end.line: How many cans do you drink a week?

description: Can by can: what a day of nothing but soda does to your blood sugar, teeth, weight and sleep.

facts.claim: A 12-ounce can of regular cola contains about 39 g of sugar, roughly 10 teaspoons.
facts.source: CDC (Rethink Your Drink) / Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

facts.claim: Sugary drinks raise blood glucose quickly, and the pancreas releases insulin in response.
Sugar and acids in soft drinks can erode tooth enamel and lead to cavities.
A 12-ounce regular cola has about 140 to 150 calories; frequent sugary drinks are linked to weight gain.
A 12-ounce cola has about 30 to 40 mg of caffeine (six cans ~ two cups of coffee); caffeine late in the day can disrupt sleep.
facts.source: Mayo Clinic (caffeine content chart) / Sleep Foundation
